name: Image Complexity
description: More complex images (e.g., high texture, many objects, low contrast) take longer to analyze by both humans and the classifier. This is the most likely explanation for multimodal distributions – distinct complexity levels create distinct processing times. This is fundamental.

name: Target Size/Scale
description: Smaller or distant targets require more processing time for both human analysts and the classifier to identify, potentially leading to distinct time groups.  It impacts feature extraction and pattern recognition.

name: Lighting Conditions
description: Poor lighting (low light, strong shadows, glare) degrades image quality, increasing analysis time for both the operator and the onboard classifier. Different lighting scenarios create different analysis demands.

name: Object Class
description: The onboard classifier might perform significantly better on certain object classes than others. Human analysis time also varies depending on familiarity and difficulty identifying specific objects.  Different classes naturally fall into different time distributions.

name: Altitude
description: Higher altitudes often result in lower image resolution or more distorted images, increasing analysis time. Lower altitudes could introduce occlusion or require more detailed scans.

name: Time of Day
description: Changes in ambient light throughout the day impact image quality and can influence both human and classifier performance, leading to varying processing times. Connected to lighting, but specifically time-dependent.

name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, fog, snow, or haze reduce visibility and image quality, increasing processing time.  Severe conditions might trigger different analysis strategies.

name: Ground Surface Type
description: Different ground surfaces (e.g., water, forest, urban) might create distinct image characteristics that influence classification and human analysis. Textural differences significantly affect processing time.

name: UAV Speed
description: Higher speeds might introduce motion blur or reduce image quality, increasing analysis time.  Lower speeds allow for more stable, clearer images.

name: Image Rotation/Orientation
description: If images are significantly rotated or require preprocessing to correct orientation, this adds to the analysis time, especially for the classifier. Human operators may be less affected but still take longer.

name: UAV Stability
description: Vibration or instability during image capture can lead to blurry or distorted images, increasing analysis time. Directly affects image quality.

name: Operator Fatigue/Attention
description: Human analysis time is subject to variability due to operator fatigue or lapses in attention. This is less relevant for the classifier but must be considered in the overall system.

name: Communication Bandwidth
description: Lower bandwidth impacts the time to transmit the image to the operator, contributing to the overall time. Though doesn't affect classifier time directly, it affects the overall mission time being optimized.

name: Sensor Quality/Calibration
description: Variations in sensor performance (e.g., due to calibration drift or manufacturing differences) can affect image quality and therefore analysis time.

name: Waypoint Type
description: Certain waypoints might be designated for specific targets, biasing the expected object classes and therefore analysis times.  For instance, a waypoint over a field of crops will have different expected image features than one over a city.
